comments.author: @MLWitteman
comments.text:
Fun fact. Besides the EU, there’s another supranational organization in Western Europe: Benelux. The area what is historically known as the Low Countries, is the region where you can find the Benelux. Benelux was formed in 1944 by the exiled governments of Belgium, the Netherlands & Luxembourg. The name is a syllabic abbreviation formed from the initial syllable of each country's name and was first used to name the customs agreement that initiated the union. 

Initially, the purpose of cooperation among the three partners was to put an end to customs barriers at their borders and ensure free movement of persons, capital, services, and goods between the three countries. This treaty was the first example of international economic integration in Europe since the Second World War.

The three countries therefore foreshadowed and provided the model for future European integration, such as the European Coal and Steel Community, the European Economic Community (EEC), and the European Community–European Union (EC–EU). The three partners also launched the Schengen process, which came into operation in 1985.
